info.name: HRMS — Employee Gratuity (End of Service)
info.description:
End-of-service gratuity: per-employee configuration and accrued-amount calculation.

## Setup

1. Run **0. Auth → Login** — it saves `token` and `company_id` automatically.
2. Set `employee_id` to any employee in that company.

## The model

- A config row is **optional**. Without one, an employee uses the statutory preset for their country (resolved from `work_country` on their salary structure, falling back to the company's country). UAE staff accrue correctly with zero setup.
- The accrued amount is **derived on every read, never stored** — it changes daily and retroactively whenever the basis salary changes.
- Built-in schemes: **AE** (21/30 days, 1-year minimum, 2-year wage cap), **IN** (15/26 days, 5-year minimum, ₹20 lakh cap), **SA** (15/30 days on gross). Any other country accrues nothing until configured explicitly.

## Cross-border employees

When an employee's `work_country` differs from the company's country — a Dubai company with someone working from India — entitlement is a contractual question the system cannot infer. Those employees come back with `requires_decision: true`, `is_enabled: false` and a `decision_options` array. **Nothing accrues until an admin picks one.** See the cross-border examples in folder 2.

## Watch for

- UAE gratuity is legally based on **basic** salary. Records with `basic_salary = 0` return explicit `warnings[]` — surface them rather than rendering a silent zero.
- Money here is returned as JSON **numbers** rounded to 2dp (unlike the salary endpoints, where NUMERIC columns come back as strings).
- Amount-bearing endpoints are **Admin only**; `/rules` is Manager-readable.

Statutory presets encode the common interpretation of each law and are overridable per employee. Not legal advice — verify against your jurisdiction and contracts.

item.description:
Gratuity endpoints that show an amount are **Admin only** (role `0`). The `/rules` endpoints are Manager-readable.

Every field is optional. Anything omitted inherits the country preset, so this one-field call is the common case when basic_salary is not split out.

The response is the FULL recomputed GET payload — update the UI from it directly.
